source_verification_note: industry_sources entries indicate the published works that informed or directionally support each lever's savings range. Where no external benchmark was found, INTERNAL_CALIBRATION is noted. All cited sources are real publications; specific savings percentages remain internal calibrations unless the source directly cites a matching range.

condition_precedents: IoT / vibration sensors installed on critical assets (OEE impact > ₹1 Cr/year downtime risk)
CMMS / EAM updated with asset criticality classifications (A/B/C)
Maintenance technician training on condition-based protocols completed
industry_sources: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) — PAT Scheme maintenance excellence results (beeindia.gov.in) — predictive maintenance reduces downtime 12-25%
CII — Maintenance Excellence case studies (cii.in) — condition-based maintenance vs time-based benchmarks
INTERNAL_CALIBRATION — savings range calibrated from 3 India manufacturing predictive maintenance mandates

execution_playbook.step: Rank assets by criticality (availability impact × replacement cost); instrument top-20 critical assets with vibration, temperature, and oil sensors
Build ML predictive models (anomaly detection, remaining useful life) using historian and CMMS data; validate on holdout failure events
Integrate PdM predictions into CMMS (SAP PM/IBM Maximo); shift maintenance triggers from calendar to condition-based
Track OEE improvement, unplanned downtime hours, and maintenance cost per production unit; rebaseline after 6 months

diagnostic_signals.signal: Unplanned downtime >5% of scheduled production hours on bottleneck assets
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Condition-based maintenance will reduce conversion cost losses from downtime

diagnostic_signals.signal: Preventive maintenance cost >30% of total maintenance budget with >40% of PMs yielding no defect found
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Shifting to PdM will reduce unnecessary maintenance and improve OEE

diagnostic_signals.signal: Mean time between failures declining YoY for critical presses, furnaces, or CNC assets
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Asset degradation trend justifies condition-monitoring investment

required_data_fields: Asset criticality register with replacement cost and availability impact
CMMS maintenance history (work orders, failure codes, costs) ≥3 years
Historian/SCADA data for instrumented assets (vibration, temperature, pressure)
Current PM frequency schedule and inspection outcomes
Unplanned outage log with duration and production impact

condition_precedents: MRO spend classified with ABC criticality and vendor rationalisation target set
Annual rate contracts (ARCs) negotiated with empanelled MRO vendors
Min/max stock norms reset on consumption data (not rule-of-thumb)
industry_sources: Ardent Partners — AP Metrics That Matter 2024 (ardentpartners.com/ap-metrics-that-matter-in-2025/)

execution_playbook.step: Aggregate MRO spend from plant stores, purchase orders, and P-cards across all sites; classify by category (mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, safety)
Identify consolidation candidates: categories with >5 vendors and fragmented spend; build RFQ for preferred vendor agreements by category
Negotiate VMI (Vendor Managed Inventory) agreements for fast-moving C-class items with top MRO distributors; implement consignment for critical spares
Build MRO catalogue in procurement system; enforce catalogue buying; track MRO cost per site and spend under management monthly

diagnostic_signals.signal: MRO vendor count >100 per site with top-20 vendors representing <50% of spend, indicating fragmentation
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Consolidation will improve leverage and reduce procurement overhead

diagnostic_signals.signal: MRO spend outside purchase order (P-card or credit card) >20%, indicating maverick purchasing
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Catalogue discipline and VMI will reduce off-contract buying

diagnostic_signals.signal: MRO unit price variance >30% for same item across sites due to decentralised purchasing
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Group contracts will harmonise pricing across plants

required_data_fields: MRO spend by site, category, and vendor (12 months)
Purchase order vs credit card spend split
Price data for common items across sites
Current VMI and consignment arrangements
Critical vs non-critical spares classification

Prioritise energy efficiency projects by payback period (<3 years): motor replacement, variable frequency drives, compressed air, and lighting retrofit
Execute top-10 projects with investment approval; file PAT cycle designation certificate; install DECs (Designated Energy Consumers) as required
Track SEC monthly vs PAT cycle target; submit BEE annual report; prepare for ESCerts trading if target exceeded

execution_playbook.step: Reconcile GSTR-2A/2B (supplier invoices filed) vs GSTR-3B (ITC claimed) for all returns periods; identify unclaimed ITC by GST head
Investigate ITC gaps: misclassified blocked credits, supplier non-filing, and wrong GST head mapping in ERP; quantify recoverable amount
File DRC-03 or revised GSTR-3B for recoverable credits; engage with vendors who have not filed returns to resolve mismatch
Implement monthly auto-reconciliation in ERP/GSTN portal; update chart of accounts to correctly classify ITC-eligible expenses

diagnostic_signals.signal: ITC claimed as % of total GST paid <80% for input-intensive sectors (manufacturing, construction, logistics) indicating under-claim
diagnostic_signals.confirms: ITC recovery will yield direct cash refund or credit

diagnostic_signals.signal: GSTR-2A/2B vs GSTR-3B ITC mismatch >5% of eligible ITC pool
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Reconciliation exercise will identify recoverable amount

diagnostic_signals.signal: Blocked credit (Schedule II items) incorrectly claimed or ITC-eligible items incorrectly coded in ERP as non-ITC
diagnostic_signals.confirms: GL reclassification will unlock additional ITC

Prior-year tax authority ITC mismatch notices if any

condition_precedents: BOM baseline validated for top-20 revenue SKUs or material categories
Should-cost models reviewed by category owner and plant engineering
Commodity index and freight-to-plant assumptions documented
industry_sources: Hackett Group — World-Class Performance Study: Procurement Benchmarks 2024 (thehackettgroup.com/research/) — should-cost driven negotiation savings 3-8% on addressable spend
McKinsey & Company — Manufacturing Sourcing Excellence (mckinsey.com/capabilities/operations/our-insights) — clean-sheet costing for direct materials
INTERNAL_CALIBRATION — savings range calibrated from 4 India manufacturing BOM should-cost mandates

execution_playbook.step: Conduct BOM review for top-20 SKUs by revenue: map every material input to specification, supplier, unit price, process yield, and YoY cost trend
Build should-cost models for primary material categories using commodity indices, casting/forging/machining cost drivers, and benchmark specs; identify yield-loss and freight-to-plant gaps
Run competitive RFQ or renegotiation using should-cost as walk-away price; validate PPAP and BIS/FSSAI spec constraints before award
Lock indexed pricing agreements with quarterly reopeners; implement material cost variance reporting in monthly S&OP

diagnostic_signals.signal: Raw material cost as % of revenue >55% vs sector P50 benchmark indicating procurement or specification gap
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Should-cost modelling will expose closable price gaps

diagnostic_signals.signal: Material price paid >8% above should-cost or commodity-indexed benchmark for ≥3 key inputs
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Negotiation or spec reset can recover margin

diagnostic_signals.signal: No should-cost refresh in >18 months despite commodity volatility >10% on key inputs
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Stale pricing allows supplier margin creep

required_data_fields: Bill of materials for top-20 revenue SKUs with quantity per unit and unit prices
Material cost trend data (24 months) by input category
Commodity price indices for key materials (steel, aluminium, polymers, chemicals)
Process yield and scrap rates by production line
Freight-to-plant and import duty assumptions by supplier

sector_specific_levers.lever_name: Raw Material Supplier Consolidation & Rate Contracts
condition_precedents: Spend segmentation completed (top-80% suppliers identified)
Supply risk assessment signed off for consolidated supplier panel
Framework rate contracts drafted with volume rebates and SLA clauses
industry_sources: Hackett Group — Supplier Base Rationalisation Benchmarks 2024 (thehackettgroup.com/research/) — 5-15% savings from strategic supplier consolidation
ACMA — Cost Reduction Programmes (acma.in) — vendor consolidation case studies in auto ancillary sector
INTERNAL_CALIBRATION — savings range calibrated from 3 India manufacturing procurement consolidation mandates

execution_playbook.step: Segment raw material spend by supplier, category, and plant; calculate HHI and identify tail vendors contributing <2% spend each
Rationalise vendor panel to strategic tier (top 60-70% spend); migrate tail spend to framework suppliers with rate contracts and quarterly rebates
Negotiate volume-based pricing, payment terms, and VMI for top-20 material SKUs; implement supplier scorecards
Track savings run-rate, supplier OTIF, and price variance vs contract index monthly

diagnostic_signals.signal: Raw material supplier count >2× peer benchmark with >40% of vendors each contributing <1% of category spend
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Tail-spend consolidation will improve leverage and pricing

diagnostic_signals.signal: No framework rate contract on materials representing >50% of RAW_MATERIALS spend
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Rate contracts will lock in competitive pricing

diagnostic_signals.signal: Supplier HHI <0.15 indicating highly fragmented supply base with weak negotiating position
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Consolidation will restore pricing power

required_data_fields: Raw material spend by supplier, SKU, and plant (12 months)
Active contracts and expiry dates by material category
Supplier OTIF and quality rejection rates
Supplier count and spend concentration (HHI)
Volume forecast by material for negotiation leverage

condition_precedents: Alternate vendor PPAP / qualification plan approved by QA

execution_playbook.step: Identify single-source materials representing >30% of category value; map import vs domestic alternatives and qualification status
Run alternate vendor qualification (PPAP, lab testing, pilot lot) for top-5 single-source materials; document spec equivalence
Execute competitive RFQ pitting incumbent vs qualified alternate; award split-volume or full switch based on TCO
Implement dual-source inventory policy and track price variance, lead-time risk, and savings run-rate

diagnostic_signals.signal: Single-source dependency for >30% of raw material spend value creating supplier pricing leverage
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Dual sourcing will restore competitive tension

diagnostic_signals.signal: Import-dependent materials with >15% landed-cost premium vs qualified domestic alternate
diagnostic_signals.confirms: Import substitution or alternate vendor will reduce cost

Lead time and MOQ constraints by supplier
PLI or domestic-content requirements if applicable
